clue.text: Thrifty group sharing vehicle to save energy

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safely held inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a carful is as many people as fit in a car, a group sharing one vehicle
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A thrifty bunch of commuters car-pool to cut their energy bills.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests car-pooling, but the group is a single word meaning a car's load of people, with E tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful can mean prudent with money, sparing in spending, which is what thrifty describes.

clue.text: Secret desire overwhelms Romeo

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf or swamp, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to covet is to desire
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hidden longing sweeps a lover off his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo suggests Shakespeare's lover, but it is just a code word for one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert means concealed or not openly acknowledged, the same as secret.

clue.text: Take stock of freak result

indicators.note: a freak thing is abnormal and twisted out of shape, so the letters come out disordered

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An auditor is asked to make an inventory after a fluke outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take stock' sounds like doing an inventory, but stock here is livestock, and taking it means stealing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal cattle or horses, literally taking someone's livestock.

clue.text: Composition of Paganini associated with French perfume

indicators.note: a composition is something put together and arranged, so the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for French
the violinist's name, rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece by the violinist Paganini is linked to a French scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' suggests a piece of music by the composer, but it signals rearranging his name; the French abbreviation goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangipani is a tropical flowering tree, and also a perfume made from or imitating its blossom.

clue.text: Cleared obstacle limiting American power

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in on both sides, so one word encloses the rest

parts.note: let is an old word for hindrance, as in without let or hindrance
A is a standard abbreviation for American
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A hurdler got over a barrier that restricted American dominance.
explanation.walkthrough: Let survives mostly in legal phrasing and tennis, where a let is a serve that hits the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is the past tense of leap, and to clear an obstacle is to jump over it.

clue.text: Doctor claimed for her consultation

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with or falsify it, so the next word's letters are tampered with

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A GP has billed for a patient's appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person in the surgery, but it is the signal to rearrange the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical examination by a doctor, the kind of appointment a consultation names.

clue.text: Peripheral devices installing back door hiding 100 computer commands

indicators.note: to install something is to set it in place within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: computer mice are peripherals

indicators.note: back tells us to read the following word from end to start
to hide something is to keep it inside and out of view, so a letter goes within

parts.note: taken as written, to be read backwards
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Plug-in gadgets fitted with a back door conceal a hundred commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back door' sounds like a security loophole in computing, but back only turns the next word round; C sits in the middle of that, and the whole lies between MIC and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Microcode is the low-level set of instructions that implements a processor's machine commands.

clue.text: Dreadful order disregards court's contribution

indicators.note: to disregard something is to leave it out of account, so letters are dropped

parts.note: to direct is to order
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A terrible ruling ignores what the court had to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means terrible or extremely serious, a synonym of dreadful.

clue.text: They may be satisfied scream sounded more emotional to audience

indicators.note: addressed to an audience means heard by listeners, so the words count by how they sound

parts.note: to cry out is to scream
tearier means more given to weeping

explanation.surface: An actor's scream came across as more emotional to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, 'cry tearier' matches the answer; the plural definition fits because criteria are things that may be satisfied or met.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards or conditions, which are things one satisfies or meets.

clue.text: Extend personal support to include November subsequently

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in as a part, so one word holds the letter

parts.note: a leg is a part of the body that holds a person up
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet
then means afterwards

explanation.surface: A personal loan is extended to cover November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal support' reads like help for someone, but it is a body part that supports a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen is to make longer, the same as extending something.

clue.text: Prospect of finance company being charged with theft at last

indicators.note: a thing charged with something is loaded or filled with it, so one word holds the other

parts.note: Visa is the payment card company

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of theft

explanation.surface: A finance firm faces charges of stealing, a gloomy outlook for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged with theft' reads as a criminal charge, but charged here means filled.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a broad view or outlook, and a prospect is likewise an extensive view of scenery.

clue.text: One pressed to make sound agreement with one working

parts.note: an accord is an agreement or treaty
I is the Roman numeral for one, and a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone is leaned on to reach a solid deal with a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective for agreement, but it belongs to the definition: the instrument is squeezed to produce sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An accordion is a squeezebox whose bellows and keys are pushed in by the player to produce music.

clue.text: Loss of status connected with mission

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
a legation is a diplomatic mission, one rank below an embassy

explanation.surface: Someone is demoted because of their links to a failed mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegation is demotion to a lower rank or division, a downgrading in standing.

clue.text: Criminal tendency

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a natural inclination or aptitude

explanation.surface: A psychologist speaks of someone's leaning toward crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a criminal tendency, but each is a separate meaning of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As slang an adjective meaning dishonest, and as a noun an inclination or knack for something.

clue.text: In accurate correspondence, what comes before my name and after yours?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: true to the original, matching it exactly

definitions.text: what comes before my name and after yours?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word in the formal letter sign-off between Yours and the signature

explanation.walkthrough: Correspondence in the first part means agreement with an original, though it also hints at letters, which the second part is about.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means accurately or with exact fidelity, and it is the word in the formal closing of a letter.

clue.text: Give a report about what one might enjoy

indicators.note: about suggests turning things around and moving them every which way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to report on things someone might find pleasurable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enjoy' here means to possess as a right, as in enjoying privileges, not to take pleasure in.
explanation.definitionFit: A prerogative is a right or privilege, something one is said to enjoy in the sense of hold or possess.

clue.text: Old rendition of most awful passage by Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

parts.note: the worst is the most awful
an aisle is a passage between seats

explanation.surface: An old recording of the dreadful passage is performed by someone called Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of 'worst aisle' and you say the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile means former, from an earlier time, which is a sense of old as in old friend.

clue.text: French city is mainly dull and worthy

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so all but the end of the word is kept

parts.note: grey means dull or drab
noble means worthy, of high character

explanation.surface: A judgment of a French city as rather boring but respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenoble is a city in the French Alps, capital of the Isère department.

clue.text: Shade providing arm's length cover?

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap over it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: umbra is Latin for shadow, used in English for the darkest part of a shadow
an ell is an old measure of length, originally based on the forearm

explanation.surface: Something that offers shelter while keeping others at a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a shade held up at arm's length as cover. Arm's length suggests aloofness, but it is an old unit of measure.
explanation.definitionFit: This object is a collapsible canopy on a handle, held overhead as a sunshade or against rain.

clue.text: Stimulating memories of modern touring cars

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel around it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: recent means modern, of late
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: Up-to-date touring cars bring back memories of earlier models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touring cars' reads as a motor-racing class, but touring is the signal for one word going around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Reminiscent of means bringing to mind or suggestive of something remembered, so it calls up memories.

clue.text: Indonesian sailor deprived of leading part in film

indicators.note: losing the leading part means the very first letter is taken away

parts.note: Java is the most populous Indonesian island
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: An Indonesian sailor loses a lead role in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading part in film' looks like a starring role, but the leading part is just the first letter, and film is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is James Cameron's 2009 science-fiction film, for years the highest-grossing ever.

clue.text: Trial said to include case for defence

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: oral means spoken

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A court hearing that includes the defence's argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Trial, case and defence all suggest a courtroom, but case only means the word's outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or harrowing experience, a trial in the sense of a test of endurance.

clue.text: It's not unusual and not masculine

parts.note: nor means and not
M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: A nod to the Tom Jones hit It's Not Unusual, with a remark about being unmanly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first words are a famous song title, but they define the answer: what is standard is by nature not unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the standard or typical pattern, so it is precisely what is not out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Great excitement in Slough that may cause problems in Hackney

definitions.text: that may cause problems in Hackney
definitions.note: describes a disease rather than naming it

parts.note: a slough is a bog or marsh
fever is intense excitement, as in fever pitch

explanation.surface: Wild excitement in the Berkshire town of Slough that might spread to the London borough of Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough and Hackney look like English place names, a town and a London borough; here a slough is a marsh and a hackney is a breed of horse. Fever placed after swamp gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Swamp fever is equine infectious anaemia, a viral disease of horses, so it afflicts a hackney horse.

clue.text: Current article in mainstream media creating unpleasant atmosphere

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: MSM is the common abbreviation for mainstream media
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news story in the mainstream press stirs up a nasty mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current article' reads as today's news item, but each word stands for a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasm, or miasma, is a noxious vapour, and figuratively an oppressive or unwholesome atmosphere.

clue.text: Great sporting occasion involving cycling

indicators.note: cycling suggests going round in a loop, so letters move from the front of the word to its back

parts.note: a game is a sporting event

explanation.surface: A big sporting event that includes a bike race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like the sport on show, but it means moving the first two letters to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang meaning huge or excellent, an informal synonym of great.

clue.text: She performs part of footballer in academy

indicators.note: part of signals that only a stretch of the following word is used

parts.note: the last six letters of the word
taken as written
A is a standard abbreviation for academy

explanation.surface: A footballer plays a role at a sports academy.
explanation.walkthrough: A footballer suggests a man on the pitch, but the definition is the female performer the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer, a woman who performs on stage.

clue.text: Drunk man is flexible

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A drunk fellow becomes loose-limbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and bending easily, which is what being flexible describes.

clue.text: Issue English staff had

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
to man something is to staff it
to have a meal is to eat it, so had can mean ate

explanation.surface: A problem that arose with the English workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a noun, a problem, but it is the verb meaning to come out.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or originate from a source, the same as to issue as a verb.

clue.text: Test introduced by prime minister related to public office

parts.note: Theresa May was UK prime minister from 2016 to 2019
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A prime minister brings in an exam for civil servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduced by' means coming after, as a speaker is introduced by the host, so the test follows the prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayoral means belonging to a mayor, the holder of a civic public office.
